Whole-class review game

Start a game

When the countdown ends, the camera pans across the room once to read every raised card — so a big class fits and each boy is counted once.

Set a class list to sweep accurately. With shared A/B/C/D cards the camera can't tell one boy from another, so it can't add up cards seen at different points of the pan — the count is shown as "at least". Per-student cards fix this completely.

      Add a question

      Options are optional — a plain question checked against A/B/C/D works too.

      Import questions — Kahoot-style CSV

      One question per row: Question, Answer A, Answer B, Answer C, Answer D, [time], Correct — where Correct is 1–4 (or A–D). It's the Kahoot quiz-spreadsheet layout, so a Kahoot export drops straight in. Header row fine; the time column is ignored.

      Make an AI prompt — for ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude

      Paste your learning and this writes a ready-to-run prompt. Copy it into any chatbot; it answers in the exact CSV format above — paste that back into the box above and Import. No account or proxy needed.

      Questions

        Class list

        Paste one boy's name per line. Each gets his own printed cards (his id + A/B/C/D), so the camera records who answered what and keeps points. Leave this empty to play anonymously with shared A/B/C/D cards instead.

        No names? Just numbers.

        Makes a class of #1…#N — each boy gets his own printed cards with just his number, so points and the leaderboard still work without typing any names. Assign the numbers however you like (or let each boy keep his card set).

        Class

        Printable answer cards

        Field-tested: 5" cards read to about 22 feet with a fixed camera (~1" of card per ~4½ ft further). Print at 100% / actual size, not "fit to page".
